question: Why does MSTR shift from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED at $77.80, and how does zero held exposure reshape the portfolio action?

epigraph.quote: The goal is to double Bitcoin per share in seven years through the use of digital credit.
epigraph.author: Phong Le, President and CEO, Q3 2026 earnings call [4]

web_blocks.html: Eight days ago, MSTR traded at $114.41 and carried a conditional wait-for-support stance above a $79.00 stop. By November 20, the stock had plunged 32.0% to $77.80, breaching that $79.00 stop as Bitcoin slid to $58,798.98. Meanwhile, the consolidated positions ledger confirms that all prior MSTR and MSTX shares have been sold. Re-underwriting from scratch without prior-verdict bias yields a clear verdict: REJECTED for new capital, and NOT_HELD for the portfolio. [42][50][54]

web_blocks.title: The bull steelman: scale, liquidity runway, and optionality

web_blocks.html: A serious bull argues that Strategy holds unmatched corporate Bitcoin scale and near-term liquidity buffers. With 850,849 Bitcoin and $4.901 billion in USD Reserve and USD Cash as of November 15, Strategy holds roughly 38 months of runway for its $1.51 billion to $1.59 billion annual fixed charges. Its convertible debt also has no mark-to-market margin calls, and the first major cash put ($1.010 billion) does not arrive until September 15, 2027. [2][50]

Bulls also note two levers that could restore upside if Bitcoin rebounds. First, cloud subscription revenue rose 49.2% year over year in Q3 2026 to $68.59 million, backed by $576.6 million in Remaining Performance Obligations. Second, management proved willing to retire 6.262 million shares of 12% STRC preferred stock over October 26 to November 15, trimming high-cost fixed dividends. If Bitcoin rallies back above $85,000, equity leverage could lift MSTR sharply above static NAV. [2][12][50]

web_blocks.title: The bear steelman: broken flywheel, fixed-charge burn, and MSCI exit

web_blocks.html: The bear case does not require Bitcoin to go to zero; it relies on capital-structure math already visible in filings. First, at $77.80 and $58,798.98 Bitcoin, MSTR trades at 0.972x EV/BTC mNAV. Issuing Class A shares below 1.00x mNAV destroys common-share Bitcoin backing, explaining why year-to-date BTC Yield is negative 4.2% even as 9M Class A shares jumped 37.6%. During November 2 to 15, 74.7% of ATM common proceeds went to buy back STRC preferreds rather than Bitcoin. [2][12][38][50]

Second, fixed obligations and put walls compress equity resilience. Software operating cash flow remains negative before treasury interest ($79.53 million in 9M 2026), forcing Strategy to sell 6,947 Bitcoin ($431.76 million) in 9M 2026 and tap its unpledged USD Reserve for preferred dividends. Meanwhile, $1.010 billion of 2028 Convertible Notes carry a cash put on September 15, 2027, followed by $4.904 billion of 2028 puts ($5.914 billion combined 2027–2028 put wall) under an S&P 'B-' rating. With MSCI excluding MSTR in November 2026 and spot ETFs charging 0.25%, passive outflows can keep mNAV below 1.0x. [2][39][50]

web_blocks.html: The table below tests Strategy’s 12-month common-equity value across Bear (-40%), Base (+10%), and Bull (+50%) Bitcoin paths using post-MSCI exit mNAV multiples and a $1.55 billion annual fixed-charge deduction. Weighting the downside and base outcomes at 40% each against a 20% bull tail anchors our single-hinge test. [2][50][54]

web_blocks.takeaway: Both the $76.34 Base case and the $66.86 probability-weighted value sit below the $77.80 close, leaving no positive expected return at current prices. [2][50][54]

web_blocks.html: The verdict hinges on one falsifiable test: can Strategy restore positive Bitcoin-per-share yield while servicing $1.51 billion to $1.59 billion of annual fixed charges without dilutive below-NAV equity sales or Bitcoin liquidation? Right now, the answer is no. Measured from the $62.00 upper edge of a hypothetical $55.00 to $62.00 watch zone against a $48.00 floor, an unadjusted $76.34 Base fair value offers only 1.02:1 asymmetry—well below our 1.50:1 hurdle. While unadjusted $76.34 would imply 1.70:1 at the $58.50 midpoint, adjusting Base fair value to $69.25 for 10% share dilution and -$67.241 million software CFO burn drops midpoint asymmetry right back down to 1.02:1. Refusing to hedge with wait-for-support makes REJECTED (TIER_0; TREND, CASH_FLOW, VALUATION) mandatory.

Our verdict separates near-term technical trend (1–3 months), medium-term capital-structure mechanics (3–12 months), and long-term business compounding (1–5 years). Each horizon requires concrete, falsifiable filing or price triggers before MSTR can leave REJECTED status. [2][42]

web_blocks.takeaway: Every horizon aligns against committing fresh capital today: broken tape in the short run, dilutive capital mechanics in the medium run, and unproven compounding in the long run.

web_blocks.html: Action trigger (NOT_HELD / REJECTED): Maintain 0 shares and 0% portfolio allocation. Re-evaluate only if Strategy posts positive quarterly BTC Yield, stabilizes USD Reserve coverage above 36 months without Bitcoin sales, and reclaims a flattening 30-week SMA ($128.25) after forming a confirmed Stage 1 base.

web_blocks.html: Because the consolidated positions ledger shows zero MSTR and zero MSTX shares, no sale order is required. The next marginal US dollar stays 100% in cash inside an S&P 500 Downtrend (10 distribution days, 34.5% breadth above 50DMA). On our opportunity-cost screen, Stage 2 shortlist leader Eli Lilly (LLY, $1,347.11, 2.08:1 support asymmetry) remains our benchmark quality compounder at 0% allocation pending market stabilization, while outside spot ETF comparator IBIT ($33.02, Stage 4) removes MSTR's preferred-stock overhang yet remains un-investable until Bitcoin repairs its trend.

book_paragraphs: When evidence shifts decisively, discipline means updating the verdict rather than clinging to last week's anchor. On November 12, MSTR closed at $114.41 and earned a conditional wait-for-support stance above a $79.00 stop. By November 20, MSTR closed at $77.80, violating that $79.00 level as Bitcoin fell to $58,798.98. Meanwhile, the positions ledger confirms that all prior MSTR and MSTX shares have already been exited. With zero shares held, we evaluate MSTR purely on fresh-capital merit. [42][50][54]

The strongest bull case rests on balance-sheet scale and time. Strategy holds 850,849 Bitcoin plus $4.901 billion in USD Reserve and USD Cash, covering roughly 38 months of preferred dividends and debt interest. None of its $6.750 billion in convertible debt carries Bitcoin price margin calls, and the first $1.010 billion cash put does not arrive until September 15, 2027. Management has also repurchased 6.262 million shares of 12% STRC preferred stock since late October while growing cloud subscriptions 49.2% year over year in Q3. [2][50]

Yet the bear case rests on arithmetic that is already unfolding. At $77.80 and $58,798.98 Bitcoin, MSTR trades at 0.972x EV/BTC mNAV. Below 1.00x, common ATM issuance no longer compounds Bitcoin per share—it dilutes it, which explains why year-to-date BTC Yield sits at negative 4.2%. Software operations remain cash-negative before treasury interest, forcing Strategy to sell 6,947 Bitcoin in nine months and draw from its unpledged USD Reserve while MSCI prepares to drop MSTR in November 2026. [2][12][38][50]

Our 12-month scenario table puts numbers on that asymmetry. Accounting for $1.55 billion in annual fixed preferred and interest charges, the Base case (+10% Bitcoin, 0.90x EV/BTC) values MSTR at $76.34 per share. The Bear case (-40% Bitcoin, 0.70x EV/BTC) drops common equity to $9.66, while the Bull case (+50% Bitcoin, 1.15x EV/BTC) reaches $162.32. Probability-weighted value is $66.86 per share—14.1% below today's close. Even measured from the $62.00 upper edge of a hypothetical $55 to $62 watch band against a $48.00 stop, unadjusted Base asymmetry is only 1.02:1, failing our 1.50:1 hurdle; adjusting Base value from $76.34 to $69.25 for 10% dilution and -$67.241 million software cash burn drops asymmetry to 1.02:1 even at the $58.50 midpoint. [2][50][54]

Accordingly, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0) based on Trend, Cash Flow, and Valuation, and NOT_HELD for existing holdings. Do not hedge an over-leveraged Stage 4 downtrend with wait-for-support language. Keep the next marginal dollar 100% in cash while the S&P 500 remains in a Downtrend. Eli Lilly serves as a Stage 2 shortlist comparator (0% funded here), and IBIT serves as a clean spot-Bitcoin comparator (also Stage 4, 0% funded), leaving cash as the highest-value posture today.

book_callouts.title: Action Rule
book_callouts.text: Hold zero shares and zero options in MSTR. Keep 100% of marginal capital in cash until Bitcoin and MSTR form a confirmed Stage 1 base, reclaim the 30-week SMA ($128.25), and restore positive BTC Yield.
